items.prompt: Which unit is used to measure electrical resistance?

options.label: Volt
Ampere
Ohm
Watt

rubric: The ohm is the unit of resistance.
Volt is potential difference, ampere is current and watt is power.

items.prompt: Which equation states Ohm's law?

options.label: P = V / R
R = I / V
I = V * R
V = I * R

rubric: Ohm's law is V = I * R.
Distractors invert or mis-multiply the quantities.

items.prompt: What quantity does an ammeter measure?

options.label: Resistance
Current
Capacitance
Voltage

rubric: An ammeter measures current in amperes.
A voltmeter measures voltage; an ohmmeter measures resistance.

items.prompt: What does Kirchhoff's current law (KCL) state about a node?

options.label: Currents into the node sum to the currents out
Current is the same in every branch
Voltages around the node sum to zero
Current into the node is always larger than out

rubric: KCL is conservation of charge at a node.
Sum of voltages to zero is KVL, which applies to loops.

items.prompt: What is the unit of capacitance?

options.label: Henry
Coulomb
Farad
Joule

rubric: Capacitance is measured in farads.
Henry is inductance; coulomb is charge.

items.prompt: Which of the following are correct formulas for electrical power? Select all that apply.

options.label: P = I^2 * R
P = V * I
P = V^2 * R
P = V / I

rubric: P = V*I and P = I^2*R are both valid forms.
V/I is resistance, not power.

items.prompt: A student building a first circuit finds a part labelled 10 mH. She wants to know what kind of component it is and what the unit measures. Which statement is correct?

options.label: It is a battery, rated in volts of supply
It is a capacitor, rated in farads of charge
It is a resistor, rated in ohms of resistance
It is an inductor, rated in henries

rubric: Millihenry (mH) is a unit of inductance, so it is an inductor.
Confusing the unit with capacitance is a common slip.

items.prompt: A 6 V battery is connected across a 12 ohm resistor. What current flows?

options.label: 2 A

rubric: 2 A comes from inverting the ratio; 72 A multiplies.

items.prompt: Two resistors are connected in series. How does the current through them compare?

options.label: It is larger through the smaller resistor
It is split in proportion to resistance
It is larger through the bigger resistor
It is the same through both

rubric: Series elements share one path, so current is identical.
Splitting current is behavior of parallel branches.

items.prompt: What happens to the total resistance when a second resistor is added in parallel with the first?

options.label: It stays the same
It doubles
It increases
It decreases

rubric: Parallel paths add conductance, lowering total resistance.
Increasing is the series result.

items.prompt: A 10 ohm and a 20 ohm resistor are in series. What is the total resistance?

options.label: 6.7 ohm
30 ohm
200 ohm
15 ohm

rubric: Series resistances add: 10 + 20 = 30 ohm.
6.7 ohm is the parallel value; 15 is the average.

items.prompt: A resistor carries a current of 2 A with 5 V across it. How much power does it dissipate?

options.label: 7 W

rubric: 2.5 W and 0.4 W divide instead of multiply; 7 W adds.

items.prompt: A capacitor is connected in series with a resistor to a DC source and has fully charged. Which statements correctly describe the capacitor? Select all that apply.

options.label: It acts like a short circuit
It blocks steady current
Its voltage equals the source voltage
Its current is at maximum

rubric: A charged capacitor passes no steady DC and sits at the supply voltage.
Maximum current occurs at the start of charging, not the end.

items.prompt: A student wires three identical bulbs in series to a battery. One bulb is then removed from its socket, leaving a gap in the loop. The student wants to predict what the other two bulbs do.

options.label: Only the bulb next to the gap goes out
Both get brighter because there is less resistance
Both go out because the loop is broken
Both stay the same because each has its own voltage

rubric: A series loop needs a complete path, so an open gap stops current everywhere.
Brighter or unchanged ignores that current drops to zero.

items.prompt: Two resistors of different values are connected in series to a battery. How does the current through the first resistor compare with the current through the second?

options.label: It is larger in the bigger resistor, because that resistor pulls more charge
It is the same in both, because there is only one path for charge to follow
It is split between them in proportion to their resistances, like a divider
It is larger in the smaller resistor, because charge flows more easily there

rubric: In a series loop there is a single path, so the same current flows through every element.
Distractors confuse series with parallel current division or assume resistance changes the current locally.

items.prompt: Three resistors of different values are connected in parallel across a 12 V source. What can you say about the voltage across each resistor?

options.label: It is larger across the smaller resistors, because more current flows there
It is smaller across the larger resistors, because they drop less voltage
It is 12 V across each, because all branches share the same two nodes
It is 4 V across each, because the source voltage divides equally among three

rubric: Parallel branches connect to the same two nodes, so each has the full source voltage.
Distractors apply the series voltage-division idea to a parallel circuit.

items.prompt: A 100 ohm resistor already sits across a battery. A second resistor of 1000 ohms is connected in parallel with it. What happens to the equivalent resistance seen by the battery?

options.label: It stays at 100 ohms, because the larger resistor carries almost no current
It becomes 1100 ohms, because the two resistances combine by addition
It rises above 100 ohms, because there is more resistive material in the circuit
It falls slightly below 100 ohms, because the new path adds extra current

rubric: An extra parallel path always lowers the equivalent resistance below the smallest branch.
Distractors treat parallel resistors as if they added in series or assume extra resistance raises the total.

items.prompt: What does Kirchhoff's current law say about a node where several wires meet?

options.label: The power delivered into the node equals the total resistance of the wires meeting there
The current divides equally among all wires leaving the node, whatever their resistances
The total current entering equals the total current leaving, as charge cannot build up
The voltages across all the wires at the node add up to the source voltage of the circuit

rubric: KCL expresses conservation of charge at a node: current in equals current out.
Distractors confuse KCL with the voltage law, with equal splitting, or with power.

items.prompt: A capacitor in a DC circuit has been connected to a constant source for a long time. How does it behave once the circuit reaches steady state?

options.label: Like a break in the circuit, passing no current at a constant voltage
Like a battery, supplying current that keeps the circuit running
Like a wire, passing a large steady current at zero voltage
Like a resistor, passing current in proportion to its capacitance

rubric: A fully charged capacitor has constant voltage and so carries no current, acting as an open circuit.
Distractors mix it up with an inductor in steady state (a wire) or with a resistor or a source.

items.prompt: Which statements correctly describe how ideal capacitors and inductors respond to sudden changes in a circuit? Select all that apply.

options.label: The voltage across an inductor cannot change instantly
The voltage across a capacitor cannot change instantly
The current through an inductor cannot change instantly
The current through a capacitor cannot change instantly

rubric: Capacitor voltage and inductor current are the continuous (stored energy) quantities.
Distractors swap the quantities; capacitor current and inductor voltage can jump.

items.prompt: A student wires one lamp to a battery, then adds a second identical lamp in series with the first. Both lamps now glow more dimly than the single lamp did. Why does this happen?

options.label: The lamps share the current equally, so each one receives half the charge
The total resistance has increased, so the current through both lamps is smaller
The battery voltage drops when a second lamp is added, so each lamp gets less
The second lamp uses up some of the current, so less is left for the first

rubric: Series resistances add, so the same battery drives less current through both lamps, which dims them.
Distractors claim current is consumed or split, which is not what happens in a series loop.

items.prompt: A 12 V battery is connected across a 4 ohm resistor and an 8 ohm resistor in series. What is the current in the circuit?

options.label: 3 A
1 A

rubric: Total resistance is 12 ohms, so I = 12 V / 12 ohms = 1 A.
Distractors use only one resistor (3 A, 1.5 A) or a wrong total.

items.prompt: A current of 0.5 A flows through a 10 ohm resistor. How much power does the resistor dissipate?

options.label: 5 W

rubric: Distractors come from using I x R (5 W) or mishandling the square.

items.prompt: A 6 ohm resistor and a 3 ohm resistor are connected in parallel. What is their equivalent resistance?

options.label: 2 ohms
9 ohms
4.5 ohms
1.5 ohms

rubric: Equivalent = (6 x 3)/(6 + 3) = 2 ohms.
Distractors give the average, the series sum, or half of a branch value.

items.prompt: A 9 V source drives a series divider of R1 = 2 kilohms (top) and R2 = 1 kilohm (bottom). What is the voltage across R2?

options.label: 6 V
9 V
3 V

rubric: V across R2 = 9 x 1/(2 + 1) = 3 V.
Distractors swap the resistors (6 V), split equally (4.5 V) or ignore R1 (9 V).

items.prompt: At a node, 5 A flows in on one wire and 2 A flows in on another. Of the two wires leaving, one carries 4 A. What current does the other leaving wire carry?

options.label: 7 A
1 A
3 A

rubric: Current in is 7 A, so the remaining outflow is 7 - 4 = 3 A.
Distractors subtract wrongly or add all currents together.

items.prompt: A 12 V source is connected across a 6 ohm resistor, giving a current of 2 A. Which calculations correctly give the power dissipated? Select all that apply.

options.label: P = V x I = 12 x 2 = 24 W
P = V x R = 12 x 6 = 72 W

rubric: Both V^2/R and V x I give 24 W.
Distractors use formulas with wrong units, such as V x R or V / R (which is current).

items.prompt: A hobbyist builds a simple timing circuit where a capacitor of 100 microfarads charges through a 10 kilohm resistor from a DC supply. She wants to estimate the time constant of the circuit, which sets how fast the capacitor charges. What is the time constant?

options.label: 1 s

rubric: Distractors come from unit-conversion slips with kilo and micro prefixes.

items.prompt: A 12 V source feeds a 100 ohm resistor in series with a parallel pair of 300 ohm and 600 ohm resistors. What current flows through the 300 ohm resistor?

options.label: 40 mA
20 mA

rubric: Parallel pair is 200 ohm, total 300 ohm, so I = 40 mA; the pair drops 8 V, and 8 V / 300 ohm = 26.7 mA.
40 mA is the total current, wrongly assigned to one branch; 13.3 mA is the 600 ohm branch current.

items.prompt: A 10 V source drives a divider of two 1 kohm resistors in series. A 1 kohm load is then connected across the lower resistor. What is the voltage across the load?
rubric: The lower resistor and load in parallel give 500 ohm; 10 V x 500/1500 = 3.33 V.
5.00 V ignores the loading effect of the load on the divider.

items.prompt: A 10 kohm resistor charges an initially empty 47 uF capacitor from a 12 V source. What is the capacitor voltage after 0.47 s?
rubric: 0.47 s equals one time constant, where the capacitor reaches 63.2% of 12 V, about 7.6 V.
4.4 V is the 36.8% remaining fraction, confused with the charged fraction.

items.prompt: A 4 ohm and a 6 ohm resistor are connected in parallel across a 12 V DC source. What total power does the pair dissipate?
rubric: Equivalent resistance is 2.4 ohm, so P = 144/2.4 = 60 W (36 W + 24 W).
36 W and 24 W are the powers of single branches, not the total.

items.prompt: A 40 ohm resistor is in series with a 100 mH inductor across a 120 V rms, 50 Hz supply. What is the approximate rms current?
rubric: XL is about 31.4 ohm; |Z| = sqrt(40^2 + 31.4^2) = 50.9 ohm, so I = 2.36 A.
1.68 A adds R and XL directly; 3.00 A ignores the inductor.

items.prompt: A 9 V DC source drives 1 kohm, 2 kohm and 3 kohm resistors in series. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

options.label: The voltage across the 2 kohm resistor is 3 V.
The circuit current is 1.5 mA.
The 1 kohm resistor dissipates 2.25 mW.
Each resistor drops 3 V because the source divides equally.
The current through the 3 kohm resistor is 3 mA.

rubric: Total 6 kohm gives 1.5 mA; V2 = 3 V; P1 = (1.5 mA)^2 x 1 kohm = 2.25 mW.
Series current is the same everywhere, and the 3 kohm drop is 4.5 V, so the other two statements fail.

items.prompt: A technician powers an LED from a 5 V supply. The LED has a forward drop of about 2 V and should carry 15 mA. A series resistor limits the current. Which resistor value should be chosen?

options.label: 133 ohm
200 ohm
333 ohm
467 ohm

rubric: The resistor must drop 5 - 2 = 3 V at 15 mA, so R = 200 ohm.
333 ohm uses the full supply voltage and 133 ohm uses only the LED drop.

items.prompt: Three equal resistors R1, R2, R3 are in series across a 12 V supply and nothing conducts. A voltmeter across R2 reads 12 V. What is the most likely fault?

options.label: R3 is shorted, so extra current overloads R2 and raises its drop
R2 is shorted, so it takes the whole supply voltage across it
R2 is open, so all 12 V drops across it and no current flows
R1 is open, so the supply voltage appears across R2 instead

rubric: With an open in a series loop, there is no current, so the open element carries the whole supply voltage.
A shorted element reads 0 V, and an open elsewhere would leave 0 V across R2.

items.prompt: A nominal 12 V battery reads 12.0 V with no load but 11.4 V while supplying 2 A to a resistor. What best explains the drop?

options.label: An internal resistance near 0.3 ohm drops 0.6 V at 2 A
The connecting current meter adds a fixed 0.6 V drop in the loop
The battery EMF falls by 0.6 V whenever any current is drawn
The load resistor dissipates part of the voltage before it reaches the terminals

rubric: 0.6 V / 2 A = 0.3 ohm of internal source resistance in series with the load.
The other options misattribute a current-dependent drop to the load, EMF, or an instrument.

items.prompt: A student finds the response of a circuit with one voltage source and one current source by superposition. To get the voltage source's effect, she replaces the current source with a short circuit. What is wrong?

options.label: The current source should be replaced with an open circuit
The current source should be replaced with its internal resistance in series
The current source should stay in place, because it supplies a fixed current
The voltage source should be shorted too, leaving the circuit unpowered

rubric: A zeroed current source carries no current, which is an open circuit; zeroed voltage sources become shorts.
The student has mixed up the two replacement rules.

items.prompt: A 120 V, 60 W lamp and a 120 V, 100 W lamp are wired in series across a 120 V supply. Which statement correctly compares them?

options.label: The 60 W lamp is brighter, because its higher resistance gives more I^2R
The 100 W lamp is brighter, because its higher power rating means it draws more current
Both are equally bright, because they carry the same current through them
The 100 W lamp is brighter, because it has a larger voltage drop across it

rubric: The 60 W lamp has about 240 ohm versus 144 ohm; with equal series current, P = I^2R is larger in the 60 W lamp.
Ratings apply at full voltage only; equal current does not mean equal power.

items.prompt: A source has a Thevenin equivalent of 12 V and 4 ohm. The load is changed from 4 ohm to 8 ohm. How does the load power change, and why?

options.label: It doubles, because the load voltage doubles when the load resistance doubles from 4 ohm to 8 ohm
It rises, because a larger resistance always dissipates more power when the source voltage is fixed at 12 V
It falls slightly, because current drops from 1.5 A to 1 A while load voltage rises only from 6 V to 8 V
It stays at 9 W, because the source voltage is fixed at 12 V and the supplied power is unchanged

rubric: Power goes from 9 W to 8 W, showing the maximum at RL = Rth.
Other options ignore the source resistance's voltage division.

items.prompt: A series RC circuit is driven by a sinusoidal source of fixed amplitude. The frequency is raised substantially. Which changes occur? Select all that apply.

options.label: The voltage amplitude across the resistor increases.
The phase angle between source voltage and current grows toward 90 degrees.
The voltage amplitude across the capacitor increases.
The capacitive reactance decreases.
The total impedance magnitude decreases.

rubric: Xc = 1/(2 pi f C) falls, so |Z| falls, current rises, and the resistor voltage rises.
The phase angle shrinks toward 0, and the capacitor's share of voltage falls.

items.prompt: In a workshop, a lamp and a motor are wired in parallel from a 120 V supply through a shared 0.5 ohm feeder cable. Each time the motor starts and draws an extra 20 A, the lamp dims briefly. What explains the dimming?

options.label: The supply's 120 V EMF falls because the motor stores energy at start
The extra 20 A creates an added drop of about 10 V in the shared feeder
The motor's start current splits and diverts part of the lamp's current
The lamp resistance drops while the motor is starting, so it gives less light

rubric: 20 A x 0.5 ohm = 10 V extra drop in the shared feeder reduces the voltage at the parallel lamp.
Parallel branches do not steal current from each other directly; the shared resistance couples them.

items.prompt: A 12 V source feeds R1 = 100 ohm in series with a parallel pair R2 = 200 ohm and R3 = 200 ohm. Replacing R3 with a 20 ohm resistor raises the power dissipated in R1. Why?

options.label: The parallel pair's resistance rises, so more voltage drops across it and R1 sees more
The parallel pair's resistance drops, so total resistance falls and series current rises
R1 receives the extra current that R3 can no longer carry because its smaller resistance blocks flow
The voltage across R1 rises because the smaller resistor in parallel adds its own voltage to the source

rubric: Lowering R3 lowers the parallel equivalent, so total resistance falls and series current (and R1 power) rises.
Distractors misread parallel resistance direction or claim voltages add in parallel.

items.prompt: In a series RC circuit driven by a 1 kHz sine wave, the capacitor voltage amplitude is measured as much smaller than the resistor voltage amplitude. What does this indicate about the circuit?

options.label: The capacitor's reactance is much larger than R at 1 kHz, so most of the source voltage drops across C
The capacitor's reactance is much smaller than R at 1 kHz, so R dominates the impedance
The capacitor's current is much smaller than the resistor's current, so it develops less voltage across it
The capacitor has charged fully, so its current is zero and it carries no voltage at 1 kHz

rubric: In series, voltage divides in proportion to impedance magnitude; a small Vc means Xc is much less than R.
Distractors reverse the divider logic or invoke DC steady state, which does not apply to AC.

items.prompt: A node-voltage analysis gives currents leaving a node as 2 A through one branch and 3 A through another, with one known source of 4 A entering. The third branch current is unknown. What is the current in the third branch, and in which direction?

options.label: 9 A leaving the node, since all known currents add together
5 A entering the node, since the two branches sum to that value
1 A leaving the node, since entering and leaving currents must balance
1 A entering the node, since the total leaving exceeds what is supplied

rubric: KCL: 4 A in = 2 + 3 + I out gives I = -1 A, i.e. 1 A entering; check: 2+3=5 leaves, 4 enters, so 1 A must enter.
Distractors mishandle the signs of KCL; the correct option must be re-read carefully.

items.prompt: A 9 V battery with unknown internal resistance powers a load. With the load connected, the terminal voltage reads 8.0 V and the circuit current is 1 A. Which statement correctly analyses the circuit?

options.label: Internal resistance is 1 ohm and load resistance is 8 ohm, since 1 V drops internally and 8 V across the load at 1 A
Internal resistance is 8 ohm and load resistance is 1 ohm, since the terminal voltage equals the drop across the internal resistance
Internal resistance is 1 ohm and load resistance is 9 ohm, since the full EMF appears across the load at 1 A
Internal resistance is 0.125 ohm and load resistance is 8 ohm, since the internal drop is the terminal voltage divided by 8 ohm

items.prompt: A 10 mH inductor in series with a 50 ohm resistor is connected to a DC supply by a switch. Right after closing, the current is near zero and then rises. Which statement explains the initial behavior?

options.label: The inductor opposes a sudden current change, so its voltage initially equals the supply
The resistor drops the full supply voltage at first, so the inductor's magnetic field must build before any current flows
The inductor stores charge on its plates, which must fill before current can flow through the circuit
The inductor acts as a short circuit at first, so current jumps to V/R immediately

rubric: Inductor current cannot change instantly; initially it behaves like an open circuit holding the full supply voltage.
Distractors confuse inductor with capacitor or reverse short/open behavior.

items.prompt: A series RLC circuit is driven at its resonant frequency. Which observations follow from the analysis of this circuit? Select all that apply.

options.label: The inductive and capacitive reactances have equal magnitude, so their voltages cancel in the series loop
The total impedance is at its minimum and equals R, so the current is at its maximum for a given source voltage
The current is 90 degrees out of phase with the source voltage because the reactances are at their peak
The voltage across R is zero because the inductor and capacitor voltages cancel each other

items.prompt: A technician builds a voltage divider from two 10 kohm resistors on a 10 V supply and expects 5 V at the midpoint. A multimeter with 1 Mohm input resistance reads 4.98 V, but a cheap meter with 100 kohm input reads 4.76 V. What best explains the difference?

options.label: The upper resistor heats up when the meter's current range is selected, changing its resistance value
The cheap meter's resistance adds in series with the lower resistor, so extra voltage drops across the meter
The meter loads the lower resistor, and its parallel resistance lowers the divider's output
The supply voltage sags more when a lower-resistance meter draws current, so the whole divider drops

rubric: 100 kohm in parallel with 10 kohm is about 9.09 kohm... in this case the effect is more severe, and the loading explains the drop.
Distractors treat the meter as series or blame the supply or resistor.

items.prompt: You must drop 5 V from a 12 V rail to supply a 20 mA sensor. Criteria: minimise wasted power and keep the output stable if sensor current varies. Which approach best meets these criteria?

options.label: Use a two-resistor divider with high values to save current
Use a series resistor, since it has no active parts and a fixed drop
Use a divider with low values so its current dominates the load variation
Use a switching or linear regulator, accepting its small quiescent current

rubric: A regulator holds the output despite load changes with small overhead; a series resistor varies with current.
Dividers and resistors give load-dependent voltage or waste power.

items.prompt: A 100 W heater is designed for 120 V. Criteria: stay safe and deliver the intended power. A colleague proposes connecting it to a 60 V source to be 'safer'. Which critique is most accurate?

options.label: Power stays 100 W because the heater draws more current to compensate
Power rises because lower voltage means lower resistance
Power falls to about 25 W since P = V^2/R with R fixed, so it underperforms
Power falls to 50 W because power is proportional to voltage

rubric: With R fixed, halving V quarters P (P = V^2/R).
Distractors assume linear scaling or constant power.

items.prompt: Two designs bypass a supply rail: one uses a 100 nF ceramic capacitor beside the chip, the other places one 1000 uF electrolytic far away at the board edge. The goal is suppressing fast current spikes at the chip. Which judgement is best?

options.label: The electrolytic is better because its long trace adds helpful resistance
The nearby ceramic is better because it has low series inductance and short traces
They are equivalent since both store charge at the same voltage
The large electrolytic is better because more capacitance always means better filtering

rubric: Parasitic inductance and trace length limit high-frequency response; local ceramic wins.
Distractors rely only on capacitance value.

items.prompt: You need a 150 ohm resistance and have only three 100 ohm resistors, all of which must be used. Which arrangement meets the requirement exactly?

options.label: All three in series, giving 300 ohm
Two in series, in parallel with the third, giving 66.7 ohm
All three in parallel, giving 33.3 ohm
Two in parallel, in series with the third, giving 150 ohm

rubric: Others give 300, 33.3, or 66.7 ohm.

items.prompt: An LED needs 20 mA at a 2 V forward drop. The supply may vary from 4.5 V to 5.5 V. The LED current must never exceed 30 mA. Which of these series resistors meets that requirement?

options.label: 47 ohm
68 ohm
120 ohm
100 ohm

rubric: At 5.5 V, 3.5/120 = 29 mA, within limit; smaller values exceed 30 mA.
Distractors use nominal supply without worst-case.

items.prompt: For a precision measurement of a 1 mV signal from a 10 kohm source, which design judgements are sound? Select all that apply.

options.label: Consider that the source resistance forms a divider with the input
Keep leads short to reduce picked-up noise
Choose a meter input resistance much greater than 10 kohm
Choose a meter input resistance near 10 kohm so the source and meter are matched for maximum signal

rubric: High input impedance, short leads and awareness of divider effects reduce error.
A large series resistor adds loading error.

items.prompt: A team picks a fuse for a 12 V circuit that normally draws 3 A with 10 A startup surges lasting 50 ms. Criteria: protect wiring rated 8 A continuous, and avoid nuisance blowing. Which fuse is best?

options.label: A 7.5 A slow-blow fuse, tolerating brief surges but protecting the wire
A 15 A fast-acting fuse, since it clears the 10 A surge with margin and still limits fault current
A 20 A slow-blow fuse, since it rides through surges and gives margin for all load conditions
A 3 A fast-acting fuse, since it matches the running current and gives the tightest protection

rubric: Slow-blow tolerates surges and 7.5 A is below the wire limit.
Others nuisance-trip or exceed wire rating.

items.prompt: Two equal resistors R form a divider from 12 V that gives 6 V unloaded. A 10 kΩ load will be attached to the output. Criteria: no active parts, output within 2% of 6 V when loaded, total dissipation under 0.5 W. Which R (each) meets all criteria?

options.label: R = 100 kΩ each
R = 330 Ω each
R = 1 kΩ each
R = 100 Ω each

rubric: With 330 Ω the loaded output is about 5.90 V (1.6% low) and the total power is about 0.22 W.
100 Ω loads the divider least but dissipates about 0.72 W; 1 kΩ gives about 5% error; 100 kΩ is loaded heavily.

items.prompt: A designer claims that doubling the series resistor R used to charge an initially empty capacitor C from a fixed voltage V will halve the energy wasted as heat. Which critique is best?

options.label: Right in part: a larger R cuts the peak current so heat falls, but only until R approaches V divided by the maximum current
Wrong: doubling R doubles the loss, because power I²R doubles while the charging time stays unchanged
Wrong: the resistor dissipates ½CV² whatever R is, equal to the energy stored, so R only sets the charging time
Right: the loss is I²R integrated over time, and doubling R halves the current, so the heat is halved

rubric: Charging through any R from a fixed source dissipates ½CV² in the resistor, because a larger R lowers current but lengthens the charge time.
Distractors treat I²R at a fixed time or current, ignoring that the charging time scales with R.

items.prompt: A 12 V relay coil is switched by a transistor rated 40 V. Criteria: the turn-off spike must keep the transistor below 40 V, the relay should release faster than with a plain flyback diode, and no extra current may flow while the relay is energised. Which snubber is best?

options.label: A plain diode across the coil, clamping the spike to about 12.7 V while the coil current decays slowly
A diode in series with a 47 V zener across the coil, releasing fastest but letting the transistor reach about 60 V
A 100 Ω resistor across the coil, limiting the spike to a modest value but drawing current whenever the coil is on
A diode in series with a 24 V zener across the coil, clamping near 37 V so the coil current decays faster

rubric: Diode plus 24 V zener clamps the transistor at about 12 + 24 + 0.7 V, under 40 V, and dissipates the coil energy faster than a plain diode.
The plain diode is slow, the resistor wastes power continuously, and the 47 V zener violates the transistor rating.

items.prompt: A source has a Thevenin equivalent of 12 V in series with 4 Ω. Criteria: load power must be at least 80% of the maximum the source can deliver, and efficiency (load power over total power) should be as high as possible. Which load resistor is best?

options.label: 4 Ω
6 Ω

rubric: Power is at least 80% of maximum for loads between about 1.5 Ω and 10.5 Ω, and efficiency rises with load resistance, so 10 Ω is the best.
4 Ω gives only 50% efficiency and 6 Ω gives 60%; 16 Ω delivers only 64% of maximum power.

items.prompt: A 50 Hz load (R in series with L) on a fixed-voltage supply has a lagging power factor of 0.7. Criteria: raise the power factor close to unity, keep the load voltage and real power unchanged, and add no real dissipation. Which correction is best?

options.label: An inductor in series with the load, adding reactance so the current lags by a smaller angle
A capacitor in series with the load, cancelling its inductive reactance so the line current falls and the load keeps its supply
A capacitor in parallel with the load, supplying its reactive current locally so the line current falls
A resistor in parallel with the load, adding real current so the total current's phase angle shrinks

rubric: A parallel capacitor leaves the load voltage and current untouched and supplies the reactive current locally, without real dissipation.
A series capacitor changes the load voltage and current, a parallel resistor wastes real power, and a series inductor increases the lag.

items.prompt: A colleague analyses a linear circuit containing two independent sources and one dependent source using superposition. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

options.label: The power in a resistor cannot be found by adding the powers each source produces alone, because power is quadratic in current
An independent voltage source is replaced by a short circuit and an independent current source by an open circuit when it is turned off
Superposition still holds when a conducting diode is present, as long as each source is applied separately
The dependent source must also be turned off in each step, just like the independent sources

rubric: Superposition applies to linear quantities (voltage, current) and not to power; deactivated voltage sources become shorts and current sources become opens.
Dependent sources must stay active, and a diode makes the circuit nonlinear.

items.prompt: A 12 V, 5 A load sits 20 m from its supply on a two-wire copper cable, so the round trip is 40 m (resistivity 0.0175 Ω·mm²/m). Criteria: total cable voltage drop of at most 3% of 12 V, using the smallest standard cross-section that meets it to save cost. Standard sizes are 4, 6, 10 and 16 mm². Which cable is best?

options.label: 4 mm²
10 mm²
16 mm²
6 mm²

rubric: The limit is 0.36 V, so R must be at most 0.072 Ω; 10 mm² gives 0.07 Ω (0.35 V drop), the smallest cross-section that qualifies.
4 mm² and 6 mm² drop about 0.88 V and 0.58 V; 16 mm² works but costs more than necessary.

items.prompt: From a 12 V supply, design a resistor divider (R1 from supply to output, R2 from output to ground) whose Thevenin equivalent at the output is 3 V in series with 750 Ω. Which pair works?

options.label: R1 = 9 kΩ, R2 = 3 kΩ
R1 = 1 kΩ, R2 = 3 kΩ
R1 = 3 kΩ, R2 = 1 kΩ

rubric: Vth = 12·R2/(R1+R2) = 3 V needs R1 = 3·R2, and Rth = R1∥R2 = 750 Ω then gives R2 = 1 kΩ and R1 = 3 kΩ.
Other pairs satisfy only one condition or neither: 1 kΩ/3 kΩ gives 9 V; 9 kΩ/3 kΩ and 1.5 kΩ/500 Ω give 3 V but the wrong Rth.

items.prompt: A source with 1 kΩ output resistance drives a passive RC low-pass filter feeding a negligible load. Using C = 10 nF, which series resistor added after the source gives a −3 dB frequency of 1 kHz?

options.label: 149 kΩ

rubric: The total R is 1/(2π·1000·10 nF) ≈ 15.9 kΩ, and subtracting the 1 kΩ source resistance leaves about 14.9 kΩ.
15.9 kΩ ignores the source resistance; the others are order-of-magnitude slips.

items.prompt: A timer uses a 100 µF capacitor charged from 0 V through a resistor from a constant supply. It must reach 2/3 of the supply voltage after 10 s. Which resistor should be chosen?

options.label: 100 kΩ
240 kΩ
91 kΩ
43 kΩ

rubric: 100 kΩ treats t as one time constant (63%); 43 kΩ uses ln 10; 240 kΩ uses ln 1.5.

items.prompt: Design an RC lag network with the output taken across the capacitor so that the output lags the input by 60° at 1 kHz, using C = 100 nF. Which resistor is required?
rubric: The lag is atan(ωRC), so R = tan 60°/(2π·1000·100 nF) ≈ 2.76 kΩ.
1.59 kΩ gives 45°, 919 Ω inverts the tangent ratio (about 30°), and 3.18 kΩ doubles the 45° value (about 63.4°).

items.prompt: A 24 V supply must power a 5 V, 1 A load. Constraints: overall efficiency of at least 80% and no isolation needed. Which designs satisfy the constraints? Select all that apply.

options.label: A buck converter at 92% efficiency delivering 5 V
A 19 Ω series resistor between the supply and the load
A 5.1 V zener shunt regulator fed through a series resistor
A linear regulator dropping 24 V straight to 5 V
A 92% efficient buck converter to 5.5 V followed by a low-dropout linear regulator to 5 V

rubric: The buck converter gives about 92% and the buck plus LDO about 84% (0.92 × 5/5.5), both above 80%.
The linear regulator is about 21% efficient; the series resistor and zener shunt also waste most of the power.

items.prompt: A 24 V supply is switched onto an uncharged 2200 µF capacitor bank. The switch contacts tolerate at most 10 A peak, and the bank must reach about 95% of 24 V (three time constants) within 0.5 s. A series resistor will be added. Which value meets both constraints?

options.label: 1 Ω

rubric: Peak current 24/R ≤ 10 A needs R ≥ 2.4 Ω, and 3RC ≤ 0.5 s needs R ≤ about 76 Ω, so 10 Ω fits.
1 Ω gives 24 A peak; 100 Ω and 470 Ω take about 0.66 s and 3.1 s to reach 95%.
